endorsements.quote: These measures should be accompanied by robust crisis detection and escalation pathways that enable rapid connection to human support when risk signals emerge.
Frontier AI laboratories should conduct mental health safety benchmarking and audit models for psychogenic risks, including sycophancy, prior to public deployment.
Chatbot applications also need to include transparent risk communication about AI limitations, including when and why safeguards are activated.

unlisted_practices: Routinely assess chatbot use when evaluating new-onset psychosis, affective instability or behavioural problems.
Assess chatbot use beyond frequency to capture purpose, degree of anthropomorphisation, epistemic trust, and clustering around insomnia, intoxication or acute stress.
Consider reviewing chat excerpts with patients to understand reinforcement dynamics.
Prioritise pragmatic harm reduction for early intervention, including structured limits on use, sleep restoration, substance use reduction and strengthening of human supports.
Involve families and carers in safety planning, with guidance on early warning signs such as social withdrawal and mood changes.
Enable platforms to detect high-intensity engagement patterns and introduce proportionate safeguards such as break prompts and sleep nudges.
Treat AI safety as a life cycle obligation including pre-deployment evaluation, post-deployment monitoring and adverse event reporting with iterative updates.
Conduct research to identify risk factors, clarify mechanisms and test prevention strategies for AI psychosis.

screen.reason: Commentary/conceptual paper proposing mechanisms for AI-induced psychosis and suggesting clinical, design, and regulatory mitigation strategies.
